newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - Mar 18.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - Mar 18.

text.p: THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

A revolt by the Papua New Guinean military yesterday wiped nearly 10 per cent from the value of Papua New Guinea-related stocks. RTZ-CRA, one of PNG's largest investors, was worst hit with more than A$235 million slashed from the stock maket value. Page 5.

After posting a A$15.4 million after-tax profit for the six months to December, the first substantial profit after a number of losses resulting from restructuring, Ken Harris, the managing director of defence manufacturer ADI Ltd, says the company is back on its feet and is now ready for privatisation after completing a major makeover of its operations. Page 19.

Lawrence Hudson, a managing director of the London-based Bankers Trust International, said in Sydney yesterday that the A$69 million Rural Property Trust has performed poorly for at least the past five-and-a-half years, with no signs of management rectifyng the situation, and he called for the removal of the trust's manager, Rural and Agricultural Management. Page 19.

Following an on-going dispute between Casinos Austria International Ltd and licensee company Christmas Island Resorts, which is headed by Indonesian businessman Robbie Sumampow, the Howard Government is moving quickly to appoint an administrator to run the Christmas Island casino after the operation closed last weekend when Casinos Austria terminated its agreement. Page 21.

The Seven Network Ltd and its partners in the embattled Optus Vision cable-TV group, Optus Communications, US West and Kerry Packer's Publishing & Broadcasting Ltd, agreed yesterday to extend until Thursday a deadline by which the partners would have to tansfer their 98 per cent stake in Vision to Seven. Page 21.

Following on-going tension between members of the Ainsworth family, the controllers of Aristocrat Leisure Ltd, and a complaint that Aristocrat is in breach of Australian Stock Exchange continuous disclosure laws, Aristocrat shares closed four cents weaker yesterday at A$2.94. Page 21.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Lawrence Hudson, the managing director of London-based Bankers Trust International - the largest unitholder in the listed A$70 million Rural Property Trust with 19.6 per cent - revealed yesterday BTI will move to oust the management of RPT, Rural & Agricultural Management, within weeks. Page 21.

News of the military revolt against the Papua New Guinea Government triggered immediate selling of stocks in the country, with Australian-listed companies Orogen Minerals Ltd and Oil Search Ltd hit hardest in a A$260 million sell-off yesterday. Heavy selling yesterday resulted in the huge decrease in market value from Australian or Port Moresby-based companies listed on the Australian Stock Exchange and with major assets in PNG. Page 21.

As Mushroom Records, Australia's largest independent record label, prepares for a major push into the difficult American market, it has unexpectedly switched its distribution and manufacturing from Festival Records to music industry leader Sony Music Entetainment. Page 23.

The Australian Taxation Office has set up a task force to evaluate the tax treatment of loan deals offering small business hundreds of millions of dollars worth of tax breaks. The ATO will target the tax treatment of a range of revenue-eroding investmentloan products. Page 23.

The latest Boardroom Survey, released yesterday by the Institute of Company Directors and accounting house KPMG, has found the number of company directors with an optimistic outlook has increased greatly. The survey of 514 company directors found the number of optimistic directors jumped from 38 per cent in the December quarter to 57 per cent in the March quarter. Page 23.

Business has warned of job instability in the wake of the Federal Government's plan to cut assistance given to small exporters. A number of business representatives yesterday questioned a Senate committee hearing on the Government's commitment to developng an export culture. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Oil Search, Australia's largest pure Papua New Guinea-based group, with a market share of A$1.2 billion, was the worst hit of many Australian-listed companies with assets in PNG as investors wiped more than A$500 million off the value of the firms amid cocerns about political instability in the resource-rich country. Page 29.

As BHP's third quarter profit result - for the three months to February 28 - nears its release on Friday, analysts are predicting the Big Australian will record a net profit of between A$320 million and A$340 million - about a 50 per cent improvement on te same period last year. Page 29.

The release last week of Coles Myer's profit figures, which showed strong demand from both institutional and small investors, has lifted the giant retailer's sharemarket value by A$800 million on hopes of further improvement in its profits, and has sparke a wave of upgradings from stockbroking firms. Page 29.

Addressing the Senate committee examining the sale legislation of the Federal Government's investment bank, AIDC, Mike Hutchinson, the chief executive of the Department of Finance's Office of Asset Sales, said the Coalition would be prepared to sell AIDC' individual businesses, but would prefer to off-load it largely intact. Page 29.

As Government-owned defence manufacturer ADI celebrates a jump in profit of 25 per cent, the company is now in a strong position for its upcoming privatisation. ADI's sales revenue rose from A$232.8 million to A$290.3 million due mainly to last year's acuisition of defence communications business Stanilite Pacific. Page 31.

Poor financial performance has led unitholders in Rural Property Trust to call for a meeting to decide for the second time whether to dump Rural Agricultural Management. The trust's 19.6 per cent unitholder Bankers Trust International called for the meetng, citing continued poor financial performance. Page 31.
THE AGE

Under a A$1 billion-plus deal, expected to be announced later this week, Edison Mission looks set to acquire full ownership of the Loy Yang B power station. The deal will see the Victorian Government shedding much of its electricity exposure and could lead to an improvement in the State's electricity market. Page B1.

As the sharemarket edged higher yesterday in quiet trade, eight Australian firms with exposure to the crisis-torn Papua New Guinean mining industry and oil and gas interests suffered a A$200 million shredding off their capitalisation. Hardest hit in dollar terms was BHP, operator of the Ok Tedi copper and gold project, which fell 9.9 cents to A$16.82. Page B1.

Speaking at the Toy Trade Fair in Melbourne yesterday, Alan Hesenfeld, chairman and chief executive of Hasbro, the world's second largest toy maker, said movies such as Star Wars, for which Hasbro holds the licence for the trilogy, had proven records for elling a wide range of products. Page B1.

Confidence in the Australian economy has improved since the December quarter, according to the latest survey of company directors. Released yesterday, the survey found the number of company directors with an optimistic outlook for the economy jumped from 29 per cent in December to 38 per cent. Page B3.

Settlement talks between Seven Network and its Optus Vision joint venture partners have again been extended as the parties continue to try to reach agreement on the restructuring of the local telephony and pay TV group. After talks failed on the weekend, Seven agreed to extend negotiations until Thursday. Page B3.

Significantly improved profit margins have further boosted Government plans for the privatisation of Australian Defence Industries. ADI yesterday posted a net operating profit of A$15.38 million in the six month period to December - turning around a A$1552 million loss for the corresponding period in 1995. Page B3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
